videos.script: One server can be hardened by hand. Fifty cannot, and they do not stay the same. {{fleet}} So configuration moves to one place: a description of how every machine should be, and something that puts it back. {{gpo}} On Windows that is Group Policy. Settings live in objects, linked to the domain and to folders of machines. {{order}} When two of them disagree, the order decides. Local, site, domain, OU. The last one wins. {{ansible}} On Linux you build the same thing with Ansible, for three machines with different jobs. One playbook, three results. {{drift}} Then somebody edits a workstation by hand. Check mode shows the difference, line by line. {{timer}} And a timer puts it back every hour, and leaves a line in the journal saying so.
